newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean ruling party offers debate with union.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean ruling party offers debate with union.

text.p: South Korea's ruling New Korea Party on Saturday offered an open debate with labour leaders over a controversial labour law which has sparked nationwide labour strife, a party spokesman said.
It is the first time the ruling camp offered an olive branch to labour unions who went on strike since the new labour bill was rammed through parliament on December 26.

"We are offering an open debate with union leaders to resolve the labour problem," the spokesman said. "We believe the current problem stemmed largely from misunderstandings and we want to talk to any labour leaders to resolve the matter."
The government has so far ruled out any compromise with union groups staging wildcat strikes, saying they are illegal.

Earlier on Saturday, militant workers wielding iron bars turned away police trying to arrest seven leaders of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions which has spearheaded nationwide strikes in the past two weeks.
The new law ends decades of near-total job security by allowing troubled companies to lay off workers.
